2025-06-17T13:24:52.3141064Z </pr_title>
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3141274Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3141453Z <pr_description>
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3142777Z This PR addresses the CI complexity and reliability issues by dramatically simplifying the workflow structure and providing multiple access methods for package installation.
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3144065Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3144215Z ## Problem
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3144772Z The repository had **6 CI workflow files** with significant redundancy:
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3145510Z - `build-artifacts.yaml`
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3145993Z - `build-packages-dev.yaml` 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3146495Z - `build-packages-prod.yaml`
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3147010Z - `build-packages-staging.yaml`
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3147493Z - `create-release.yaml`
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3147907Z - `tools.yaml`
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3148121Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3149221Z This created maintenance complexity and CI reliability issues, making it difficult to successfully build and access wheel artifacts.
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3150471Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3150635Z ## Solution
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3151179Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3151370Z ### 1. Consolidated CI Workflows
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3151971Z **Reduced from 6 to 3 focused workflows** (50% reduction):
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3152445Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3153142Z - **`build-and-deploy.yaml`**: Unified workflow that builds once and deploys to appropriate environments based on triggers
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3154651Z - **`commit-wheels.yaml`**: Fallback workflow that commits wheels directly to the repository when CI builds succeed
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3155824Z - **`tools.yaml`**: Unchanged, handles build tools and container management
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3156378Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3156576Z ### 2. Multiple Installation Methods
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3157108Z Users can now install packages via:
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3157445Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3157626Z **One-line installer:**
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3158028Z ```bash
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3158953Z curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgbaird/opentrons-python-packages/main/install.sh | bash -s -- pandas
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3159998Z ```
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3160182Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3160622Z **Direct wheel download:**
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3161068Z ```bash
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3162264Z curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sgbaird/opentrons-python-packages/main/wheels/pandas-1.5.0-cp310-cp310-linux_armv7l.whl -o /tmp/pandas.whl
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3163586Z pip install /tmp/pandas.whl
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3163993Z ```
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3164159Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3164417Z **CI artifacts and releases** (when CI runs successfully)
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3164860Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3165036Z ### 3. Immediate Package Access
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3166120Z Added pre-built wheel files directly to the repository in the `wheels/` directory, so packages are immediately available even if CI fails.
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3167106Z 
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3167260Z ## Key Benefits
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3167718Z - **Simplified maintenance**: 50% fewer workflow files
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3168640Z - **Eliminated redundancy**: Single build logic instead of duplicated across multiple files
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3169635Z - **Improved reliability**: Multiple fallback access methods
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3170753Z - **Better user experience**: Immediate access to packages via curl/pip as requested
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3171801Z - **Clear documentation**: Added `CI-SIMPLIFICATION.md` explaining the changes
2025-06-17T13:24:52.3172529Z

2025-06-17T13:24:52.3328962Z - `TS_OAUTH_SECRET`: Your OAuth client secret

2025-06-17T13:50:52.2143420Z   +    <h2 class="page-title">Project description</h2>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2144121Z   +      <div class="project-description"><a href="https://github.com/MagicStack/asyncpg/actions?query=workflow%3ATests+branch%3Amaster" rel=nofollow>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2145686Z   +<img alt="GitHub Actions status" src="https://pypi-camo.freetls.fastly.net/78c05e026d39952811f8bcecee4d641a8db2cb79/68747470733a2f2f6769746875622e636f6d2f4d61676963537461636b2f6173796e6370672f776f726b666c6f77732f54657374732f62616467652e737667">
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2146761Z   +</a>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2147029Z   +<a href="https://pypi.python.org/pypi/asyncpg" rel=nofollow>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2148072Z   +<img alt="https://img.shields.io/pypi/v/asyncpg.svg" src="https://pypi-camo.freetls.fastly.net/0fdabeb4a90333ef6f0491753e26b6523500e2d1/68747470733a2f2f696d672e736869656c64732e696f2f707970692f762f6173796e6370672e737667">
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2149015Z   +</a>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2149357Z   +<p><strong>asyncpg</strong> is a database interface library designed specifically for
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2149920Z   +PostgreSQL and Python/asyncio.  asyncpg is an efficient, clean implementation
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2150965Z   +of PostgreSQL server binary protocol for use with Python’s <span class="docutils literal">asyncio</span>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2151593Z   +framework.  You can read more about asyncpg in an introductory
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2152191Z   +<a href="http://magic.io/blog/asyncpg-1m-rows-from-postgres-to-python/" rel=nofollow>blog post</a>.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2152819Z   +<p>asyncpg requires Python 3.8 or later and is supported for PostgreSQL
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2153275Z   +versions 9.5 to 17.  Other PostgreSQL versions or other databases
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2153747Z   +implementing the PostgreSQL protocol <em>may</em> work, but are not being
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2154140Z   +actively tested.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2154373Z   +<section id=documentation>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2154632Z   +<h2>Documentation</h2>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2154894Z   +<p>The project documentation can be found
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2155342Z   +<a href="https://magicstack.github.io/asyncpg/current/" rel=nofollow>here</a>.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2155757Z   +</section>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2155963Z   +<section id=performance>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2156202Z   +<h2>Performance</h2>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2156565Z   +<p>In our testing asyncpg is, on average, <strong>5x</strong> faster than psycopg3.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2157134Z   +<a href="https://gistpreview.github.io/?0ed296e93523831ea0918d42dd1258c2" rel=nofollow>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2158863Z   +<img alt="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MagicStack/asyncpg/master/performance.png?fddca40ab0" src="https://pypi-camo.freetls.fastly.net/cfd9ddf54ddaa3b325b4df42aec46c44e32219c2/68747470733a2f2f7261772e67697468756275736572636f6e74656e742e636f6d2f4d61676963537461636b2f6173796e6370672f6d61737465722f706572666f726d616e63652e706e673f66646463613430616230">
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2160525Z   +</a>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2160850Z   +<p>The above results are a geometric mean of benchmarks obtained with PostgreSQL
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2161476Z   +<a href="https://github.com/MagicStack/pgbench" rel=nofollow>client driver benchmarking toolbench</a>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2162033Z   +in June 2023 (click on the chart to see full details).</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2162351Z   +</section>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2162547Z   +<section id=features>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2162770Z   +<h2>Features</h2>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2163105Z   +<p>asyncpg implements PostgreSQL server protocol natively and exposes its
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2163599Z   +features directly, as opposed to hiding them behind a generic facade
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2163972Z   +like DB-API.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2164263Z   +<p>This enables asyncpg to have easy-to-use support for:</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2164603Z   +<ul class=simple>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2164850Z   +<li><p><strong>prepared statements</strong></li>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2165308Z   +<li><p><strong>scrollable cursors</strong></li>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2165690Z   +<li><p><strong>partial iteration</strong> on query results</li>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2166127Z   +<li><p>automatic encoding and decoding of composite types, arrays,
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2166640Z   +and any combination of those</li>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2166973Z   +<li><p>straightforward support for custom data types</li>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2167292Z   +</ul>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2167469Z   +</section>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2167673Z   +<section id=installation>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2167916Z   +<h2>Installation</h2>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2168277Z   +<p>asyncpg is available on PyPI.  When not using GSSAPI/SSPI authentication it
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2168709Z   +has no dependencies.  Use pip to install:</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2169021Z   +<pre>$ pip install asyncpg</pre>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2169334Z   +<p>If you need GSSAPI/SSPI authentication, use:</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2169674Z   +<pre>$ pip install 'asyncpg[gssauth]'</pre>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2170467Z   +<p>For more details, please <a href="https://magicstack.github.io/asyncpg/current/installation.html" rel=nofollow>see the documentation</a>.</p>
2025-06-17T13:50:52.2171120Z   +</section>
